objectClass.notes: Exact official G1 EDU image set: cyan sensor helmet, tapered torso shell, exposed waist/pelvis, continuous limb armour, Dex3-1 hands. Domain is object: anthropomorphic mechanical assembly, never human anatomy.

reasoning: Official full-body and close-up references show a deep bilateral articulated hierarchy; likeness depends on continuous shell profiles, joint placement, sensor head, Dex3 hands and independent material responses.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Choose simple/moderate/complex/ultra-complex from observed structure, not from a hardcoded domain.

unknownsToResolveBeforeImplementation: Rear compute cover and cable routing require an admitted rear video frame; until then label them inferred.
Official stills mix poses, so only g1-03 and g1-05 may drive neutral proportions.
GLB proves articulation hierarchy but does not prove EDU surface materials or exact external shell topology.

details.description: Continuous cyan rounded U-shaped perimeter around dark face cavity
Single cyan horizontal sensor bar across upper face cavity; no eye pair
Graphite helmet crown extends rearward beyond narrow neck pedestal
Small black downward triangle centered high on silver chest
Curved lower torso lip with visible dark undercut above waist
Dark vertical side panel with two recesses and four green indicators
Three exposed dark waist stages with distinct diameters and seams
Trapezoidal front pelvis cover with lower tongue and perimeter fasteners
Silver circular cap centered on each rounded shoulder housing
Silver upper and lower arm link shells form sculpted S curves around joint axes
Three narrow black grooves around each wrist actuator
Two long fingers and opposable thumb with visibly separate black pads and joint pins
Circular upper thigh cap and two transverse lower seam lines
Large black circular disc mounted laterally at each knee
Perforated silver ankle bars and visible joint pins bridge shin shell to foot
Low dark shoe-like foot with raised heel and tapered rounded toe
Cool high-value silver armour with broad satin highlight and subtle fine grain
Dark actuator housings vary from fine textured semi-matte to smoother ring edges

anatomy.note: Non-biological articulated robot; proportions live in component dimensions and silhouette contracts.

definitionOfDone: At fixed official-reference cameras the model must read immediately as Unitree G1 EDU: no-eye cyan sensor helmet, single tapered silver torso shell with black triangle, exposed three-axis waist and compact pelvis, sculpted S-profile arms, continuous thigh/shin shells with lateral knee discs, exposed ankle links, long dark feet, side battery panel and correctly segmented Dex3-1 hands.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: At the fixed standing camera, total envelope is 1320:450:200 and the head/torso/pelvis/limb negative spaces match g1-03 within the silhouette hard gate.
failureModes: head reads as a box or face with eyes
torso reads as a chest screen or box
joint spheres dominate the silhouette
limb armour remains cylindrical or cuboid

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Head, neck, torso, 3-axis waist, pelvis, bilateral 5-DOF arms, bilateral 6-DOF legs, wrists, ankles and Dex3 digits are separate named scene-graph parts.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Silver armour, graphite mechanisms, black elastomer, sensor glazing and cyan emission use independent PBR channels and region-specific roughness.
No procedural dirt or wear is added because official product renders show clean surfaces.
failureModes: surface looks like flat plastic
local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

featureGroups.name: G1 sensor-head identity
qualityCriteria: Continuous helmet shell, dark recessed face cavity, cyan perimeter and one horizontal bar; no eyes.
failureModes: eyes or facial features present
cyan border disconnected
helmet rear overhang absent

featureGroups.name: G1 continuous limb shells
qualityCriteria: S-profile arm links and tapered thigh/shin shells use continuous profiles around exposed rotary joints.
failureModes: box or capsule stacks substitute continuous profiles
knee discs or ankle negative spaces absent

featureGroups.name: Dex3-1 hand identity
qualityCriteria: Each hand has two long fingers plus an opposable thumb, segmented pads and articulation pivots.
failureModes: five-finger hand used
digits are tiny sticks
palm and segment joints are fused

visualDeltaChecks: waist/pelvis/arm region against g1-06 and g1-08
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

authoringInstruction: Fill observed object class, complexity reasoning, featureGroups, visualDeltaChecks, and unknowns before generating or implementing ObjectSculptSpec.

snippets: A pivot is a local rotation origin; a socket is an attachment point for a child part. In a runtime hierarchy, a socket Object3D is a child of the relevant pivot.
